Yes, this is right. I opened the menu, chose "Delete bookmark…," and it asked me to confirm before actually removing it — which I'd want, since deleting is the kind of thing I shouldn't be able to do with one stray click. After I confirmed, that bookmark was gone and everything else — my other bookmarks and their tags — stayed exactly as they were.

Your assumptions match what I'd expect: deleting the bookmark takes its note, its tag connections, and its read-later state along with it, but a tag I still use on other bookmarks should stick around. I wouldn't want deleting one recipe to wipe out a tag I'm using elsewhere. Good — deletion itself matches my intent.

One thing I want to raise while we're here, since it's closely tied: this is the permanent, gone-for-good version, and that's correct for "Delete." But I'd also want a gentler option — a way to tuck a bookmark out of my main list without destroying it, for things I'm done with but not sure I want to lose forever. So I'd expect *two* different actions: this permanent delete, and a reversible "set it aside" that hides it but lets me get it back. Can we make sure that reversible option exists too, separate from this? Not blocking this round — the delete behavior here is right. Let's keep going.
